chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Shaybani al-Muktab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Muhammad ibn Abu Abdullah al-Kufi said: Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, on the authority of Abd al-Azim ibn Abdullah al-Hasani, on the authority of Imam Ali ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali, on the authority of his father al-Rida Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them), said:

Abu Hanifah left the presence of al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) one day, and Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) came across him and said to him: 'O young man, from whom is the insubordination (sin)?' He (AS) answered: 'It does not deviate from three possibilities: Either it is from Allah, the Mighty and High, and is not from Him, so it is not fitting for the Generous to punish His servant for something he does not acquire; Or it is from Allah, the Mighty and High, and from the servant, but this is not the case, so it is not fitting for the Strong Partner to oppress the weak partner; Or it is from the servant and is from him, so if Allah punishes him, it is because of his sin, and if He forgives him, it is due to His Grace and Generosity.'

key_terms.الشَّرِيكِ الْقَوِيِّ: The Strong Partner (referring to God in the context of shared agency)

ai.seo_question: What is the theological explanation for the origin of sin and divine justice according to Imam Musa ibn Ja'far?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* highlights the encounter between Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) and the prominent Sunni jurist Abu Hanifah, showcasing the Imam’s logical rigor in defending Divine Justice (*Adl*). By systematically eliminating the possibilities that sin originates from God or is shared with Him, the Imam establishes that sin is exclusively the act of the servant, thereby ensuring that divine punishment is just and forgiveness is purely an act of grace. This argument serves as a foundational Shia response to the Mu'tazila and Sunni schools regarding the nature of human agency and divine decree.
